narrative:
The base case assumes the NBP reference rate falls from 4.00% to 3.50% by Q4-26. VeloBank is asset-sensitive: every -100bp parallel shift removes roughly PLN 180M of annual NII, about 5.4% of the plan, inside the 7.5% IRRBB internal limit.

The dovish path (terminal 3.00%) costs a further ~PLN 90M in FY2027, concentrated in current accounts and savings, where the replicating portfolio reprices fastest. A hawkish hold at 4.00% adds a similar amount but is the least likely outcome given the MPC's guidance.

The ex-Citi deposits change the shape of the curve. Their behavioural duration is unobserved through a cutting cycle, so the scenario engine weights them conservatively until six months of VeloBank-era data exist.

signals.title: NBP Monetary Policy Council — Rate Decision
signals.excerpt: The MPC lowered the reference rate and signalled further easing as CPI returns toward the 2.5% target. Market pricing implies a terminal rate near 3.50%.

signals.title: Management Commentary — Rate Headwind
signals.excerpt: Management flagged NBP rate cuts as the key earnings headwind for net interest income, with deposit pricing discipline and balance-sheet growth as offsets.

signals.title: EBA IRRBB Supervisory Outlier Test
signals.excerpt: Banks must report ΔNII and ΔEVE under prescribed rate shocks; a ΔEVE decline above 15% of Tier 1 capital triggers supervisory dialogue.
